set.name: set
evidence: VirtualDJ 2026 (HTTP interface, 2026-07-22): 'set $v on' stores yes and 'set $v off' stores no, but 'true'/'false' are NOT constants and store nothing. Quoting decides type: 5 and '5' are different values. Storing a string makes the variable unreadable and uncomparable — use numeric codes.

var_equal.name: var_equal
evidence: VirtualDJ 2026 (HTTP interface, 2026-07-22): UNSAFE for string-valued variables — once a variable holds a string, var_equal returns 'yes' against every comparand ('apple' vs 'banana' vs bare banana all yes), so a string-keyed branch always takes the true branch and looks like it works. Correct for numeric/boolean values, where quoting is significant: with $v=5, 'var_equal $v 5'=yes but 'var_equal $v "5"'=no. Store numeric codes.

video_fx_select.name: video_fx_select
evidence: VirtualDJ 2026 (HTTP interface, 2026-07-22): '+1' cycles the enabled video-FX list (17 entries on this install); readback via get_videofx_name. By-name it accepts ANY installed effect name, audio ones included (`video_fx_select 'Echo'` really does set the video slot to Echo), so the selector is not type-restricted and loadability cannot be used to classify an effect.

video_transition_select.name: video_transition_select
evidence: VirtualDJ 2026 (HTTP interface, 2026-07-22): '+1' cycles the enabled transition list (35 entries); readback via get_videotrans_name. 'None' is a valid transition and works as a park value. Like video_fx_select it accepts any installed effect name.

while_pressed.name: while_pressed
evidence: VirtualDJ 2026 (HTTP interface, 2026-07-22): a trailing modifier, not a verb — accepted both trailing ('set $a 1 while_pressed') and mid-chain, and mid-chain it does not block the rest of the chain (both statements ran). Release behavior is untestable over HTTP (no press/release), so its actual semantics still need a pad or mapper run.
